real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to horizontally elongated bodies clearly raised on legs or wheels, seen at an angle that shows the side, which in practice means mostly road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks) seen in three-quarter or side view. It probably extends to standing quadrupeds as the original explanation claims, but these photos cannot test that.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to horizontally elongated bodies clearly raised on legs or wheels, seen at an angle that shows the side, which in practice means mostly road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks) seen in three-quarter or side view. It probably extends to standing quadrupeds as the original explanation claims, but these photos cannot test that.
parsed.evidence: The top classes are all vehicles. Within those classes, 'long body clearly raised on legs or wheels' (d +1.06, 100th percentile), three-quarter view (d +0.71, 99th percentile) and visible side including the front wheel (d +0.34, 96th percentile) raise activity, while front or rear views (d -1.05, 1st percentile) and hidden wheels (d -1.07, 0th percentile) lower it.
parsed.missing_data: Activity on dog and other quadruped photos, to check the claimed animal response, since none of the top-12 classes contain animals; also why pure side-on profiles are not favored over three-quarter views.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to a horizontally elongated body visibly raised on legs or wheels, seen from the side or at a three-quarter angle. Mainly this is the body of a road vehicle above its wheels, with a related extension to the flanks of standing four-legged animals such as dogs.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to a horizontally elongated body visibly raised on legs or wheels, seen from the side or at a three-quarter angle. Mainly this is the body of a road vehicle above its wheels, with a related extension to the flanks of standing four-legged animals such as dogs.
parsed.evidence: The elongated-and-raised question gives the strongest within-class signal: yes is d +1.06 (100th percentile), while a body with hidden or cropped wheels is d -1.07. Three-quarter views (+0.71) and whole-side views with the front wheel (+0.34) are high, front or rear views (-1.05) and front/interior views (-0.83) are low, and pure side-on profiles are not elevated (-0.14), so the 'side-profile' wording is too narrow.
parsed.missing_data: Animal photos, especially dogs standing versus sitting or lying, to test whether the raised-body selectivity carries over to quadrupeds, since this photo set contains no animals.
